question:
An aircraft flies horizontally at a constant speed of $60\ \text{m/s}$ at an altitude of $800\ \text{m}$. Let $x$ be its horizontal distance from an observer on the ground and $z$ be its straight-line distance from the observer.

(a) Form a relation connecting $x$ and $z$.

(b) Determine the instantaneous rate at which the aircraft's distance from the observer is increasing when $x=600\ \text{m}$.

(c) Find the acceleration of its distance from the observer at the same instant.
explanation:
(a)
Using the right triangle formed by the altitude, horizontal distance and straight-line distance,
$$z^2=x^2+800^2$$

(b)
When $x=600\ \text{m}$,
$$z=\sqrt{600^2+800^2}=1000\ \text{m}$$
Differentiating $z^2=x^2+800^2$ with respect to time,
$$2z\frac{dz}{dt}=2x\frac{dx}{dt}$$
Therefore,
$$\frac{dz}{dt}=\frac{x}{z}\frac{dx}{dt}$$
Substituting $x=600$, $z=1000$ and $\frac{dx}{dt}=60$,
$$\frac{dz}{dt}=\frac{600}{1000}(60)=36\ \text{m/s}$$
Thus, the aircraft's distance from the observer is increasing at $36\ \text{m/s}$.

(c)
From
$$z\frac{dz}{dt}=x\frac{dx}{dt}$$
differentiating again with respect to time gives
$$\left(\frac{dz}{dt}\right)^2+z\frac{d^2z}{dt^2}=\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)^2+x\frac{d^2x}{dt^2}$$
The aircraft's horizontal speed is constant, so $\frac{d^2x}{dt^2}=0$. Hence,
$$36^2+1000\frac{d^2z}{dt^2}=60^2$$
$$1000\frac{d^2z}{dt^2}=3600-1296=2304$$
Therefore,
$$\frac{d^2z}{dt^2}=2.304\ \text{m/s}^2$$
